Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and Sri Dilip Pandey, who has filed Vakalatnama on behalf of the complainant and perused the record.
The Vakalatnama is taken on record.
2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.89 of 2024, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station Dalmau, District Raebareli.

3. In terms of the FIR registered on 16.03.2024, it was alleged that on 16.03.2024, the sister of the informant aged about 24 years had died and this information was received by the maternal uncle of the deceased.
It was alleged that the entire matrimonial family had pushed the sister of the informant in a Atta Machine.
It was also stated that on earlier occasions also threats were extended for killing the sister of the informant.
Based upon the said, the investigation was carried out.

sentences.text:
1 time of inquest, the relatives of the deceased were present and as per the inquest report, prima faice,
a view was formed that she came in contact with the machine and received injuries.

The other statement of the independent witness, who used to go to the said shop, stated that the sisters-in-law and the brother-in-law had no dispute with the deceased and they have been wrongly implicated.
It was also alleged that the term in between the husband, the father-in-law and the mother-in-law with the deceased was not cordial and on occasions, there were altercations with regard to the dowry.
It was specifically stated that three persons in the FIR are not guilty for the offence in question.
4. In the light of the aforesaid, it is argued that the father-in-law and the mother-in-law were enlarged on bail vide separate orders dated 22.08.2024 and 31.08.2024 respectively.
He further argues that nowhere in the FIR, the allegations with regard to the harassment for dowry was levelled, as such, the applicant cannot be implicated for an offence under Section 304-B IPC.
It is also argued that the applicant is in custody since 17.03.2024 and has no criminal antecedents.

5. Learned A.G.A. as well as learned Counsel for the complainant vehemently opposed the bail prayer by arguing that although in the FIR, no allegation with regard to the demand of dowry was not levelled, however, in the subsequent statement, it was specifically alleged that the matrimonial family used to harass her for dowry and they had killed her.
My attention has drawn to the statement of the complainant, wherein, it was stated that the marriage of the applicant with the deceased was a love marriage.
It was also stated that all the matrimonial family members had killed her on account of non-payment of dowry.
A similar statement was given by the uncle of the deceased, wherein, he had admitted that both of them had married out of love in a temple in the year 2021.

6. Considering the inquest report; the postmortem report shows a crush injury present at skull and the cause of death was coma due to ante mortem head injury; prima facie, the the death had occurred on account of coming in contact with the machine; general allegations have been levelled against the entire matrimonial family without there being any corroboration coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal antecedents and is languishing in jail since 17.03.2024, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.
